extraction.name: SWE-Gym
extraction.description: SWE-Gym is the first training environment combining real-world software engineering tasks from GitHub issues with pre-installed dependencies and executable test verification. It contains 2,438 Python tasks sourced from 11 popular open-source repositories, each comprising a Python codebase with an executable runtime environment, unit tests, and a task specified in natural language.
extraction.creator: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang
extraction.publisher: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning
extraction.rai:dataCollection: SWE-Gym comprises 2,438 real-world software engineering tasks sourced from pull requests in 11 popular Python repositories. The dataset construction involved: (1) filtering Python repositories created before July 1, 2022 with >500 stars, ≥300 lines of code, >500 pull requests and 100+ contributors using SEART GitHub search, resulting in 358 repositories; (2) extracting 64,689 task instances using SWE-Bench's instance extraction script; (3) semi-manually creating executable environments for 11 repositories with numerous instances; (4) manually configuring dependencies for each task instance using configuration files, CI scripts, or documentation; (5) validating instances using execution-based validation to ensure gold patches pass more unit tests than original code. This process required approximately 200 human annotation hours and 10,000 CPU core hours.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of GitHub pull requests and issues from Python repositories. SWE-Gym Raw contains 64,689 task instances spanning 358 Python repositories, including natural language descriptions of issues, repository snapshots at the time of issue creation, unit tests, and solution code diffs (git patches). Each task instance corresponds to a GitHub issue with its associated codebase.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: GitHub issues and pull requests were extracted from repositories using SWE-Bench's instance extraction script. Each task instance corresponds to a GitHub issue with associated code repository. Correctness is verified using human-written test suites.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: SWE-Bench's instance extraction script was used to convert repositories into task instances. SEART GitHub search was used to filter initial repositories.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The task distribution across repositories exhibits a long-tail pattern, with tasks associated with pandas comprising nearly one-third of the total, whereas tasks related to bokeh represent a mere one percent.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Tasks in SWE-Gym are on average harder than those in SWE-Bench. Models have consistently lower performance on SWE-Gym compared to SWE-Bench, which may be due to the inclusion of sophisticated repositories like pandas and MONAI. Gold patches in SWE-Gym have significantly more lines and files edited compared to SWE-Bench.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: SWE-Gym is designed as a training environment for software engineering agents and verifiers, enabling scalable learning for resolving complex software tasks with repository-level context, pre-configured execution environments, and test verifications.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Filtered subset creation following SWE-Bench Lite pipeline: excludes tasks requiring editing more than one file, tasks with poorly described problem statements, tasks with excessively complex ground-truth code diffs, and tests focused on error message validation. This resulted in SWE-Gym Lite comprising 230 instances from the full 2,438 instances.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Initial repository filtering using SEART GitHub search to select Python repositories created before July 1, 2022 with more than 500 stars, at least 300 lines of code, more than 500 pull requests and 100 contributors, resulting in 358 repositories. Task instances extracted from repositories using SWE-Bench's instance extraction script, with each instance comprising a Python codebase with executable runtime environment, unit tests, and natural language task specification.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: we introduce SWE-Gym, the first training environment that addresses critical gaps in enabling scalable learning for software engineering agents. By combining real-world Python tasks with repository-level context, pre-configured execution environments, and test verifications, SWE-Gym will be a foundation for advancing LM agent training research.
